Valentine's Day Heart Sugar Cookies

Served at: Saint Valentine's Day

About 24-30 cookiesPrep 45 min (plus 1 hour chilling)Cook 8-10 min per batch

These classic heart-shaped sugar cookies are a delightful and traditional way to celebrate Saint Valentine's Day. Easy to make and fun to decorate, they are perfect for sharing with loved ones as a sweet token of affection. Their simple, buttery flavor makes them a beloved treat for all ages.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/4 cups (270 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup (226 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 1/2 cups (300 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  • For Icing (Optional):
  • 2 cups (240 g) powdered sugar
  • 2-3 tablespoons milk (or water)
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Red or pink food coloring (optional)

Method

  1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
  2. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, cream together the softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.
  3. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until well combined.
  4. Gradually add the dry flour mixture to the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed until just combined and a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
  5. Divide the dough in half, flatten each half into a disc, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour (or up to 2 days).
  6. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disc of chilled dough to about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thickness. Use heart-shaped cookie cutters to cut out shapes.
  8. Carefully transfer the cut-out cookies to the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) between them.
  9. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden. Let cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.
  10. While cookies cool, prepare the icing (if using): In a small bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla extract until smooth. Add more milk a teaspoon at a time if needed for desired consistency. Stir in food coloring if desired.
  11. Once cookies are completely cool, spread or pipe the icing onto the cookies. Let the icing set before stacking or storing.

Tips

  • For a citrusy twist, add 1 teaspoon of lemon or orange zest to the dough along with the wet ingredients.
  • Decorate with sprinkles or edible glitter before the icing sets for extra festive flair.
  • Store cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3-4 days, or freeze un-iced cookies for up to 3 months.
